name: Chip-to-chip interconnect
summary: The links that let several accelerators share work. Fast dedicated links let a group of chips act like one big chip; slower general-purpose links make them wait.

D1.guide: Two chips share one model. Guess what happens if their link is slow.
text: Big AI models are often too large for one chip, so several chips share the work.
They must keep passing notes to each other. If the note-passing is slow, the chips sit waiting instead of working.
D1.analogy: Pupils sharing one big puzzle, passing pieces across the table.

text: A model can be split across chips in two main ways. **Splitting by layers** sends each chip a run of layers, and only a small bundle of results crosses between them per token. **Splitting inside each layer** (tensor parallelism) makes every chip do part of every layer, so they swap results many times per token.

General-purpose links such as PCIe connect a GPU to the rest of the computer and are fine for the first kind of split. Dedicated chip-to-chip links (NVLink-style, or open standards such as UALink) are much faster and can join many accelerators into one shared domain, which the second kind of split needs.
Beyond one box, network fabrics join many such groups into the clusters of the layer above.

diagram.caption: General-purpose link versus dedicated chip-to-chip link

columns.title: PCIe-style link
points: Connects a GPU to the whole computer
Standard in every desktop and server
Fine when chips swap little data

columns.title: NVLink-style link
points: Much higher bandwidth, often via switches
Lets many chips act like one

D2.analogy: Passing notes across the table versus everyone writing on one shared whiteboard.
D2.analogyBreaks: Note-passing slows a little with each extra pupil. With chips, a slow link can make adding a second chip barely faster, or even slower, because every layer has to wait for the swap.

predict.question: Two GPUs connected only by PCIe run one model. Which split usually works better?
options: Each GPU does half of every layer, swapping results after each one
Each GPU takes half of the layers, passing one small result across per token
Both GPUs hold the whole model and take turns
predict.explanation: Splitting by layers sends little data across the slow link. Splitting inside every layer needs constant swaps, which is what fast dedicated links are for.

text: The size of the fast-link domain, how many chips can talk at full speed, is now a headline feature of AI systems, and vendors compete with proprietary links against open standards.

Copper links are reaching their distance limits, so optical links and co-packaged optics are being explored. Communication can also be overlapped with computation, which blurs how much a faster link actually helps a given model.

sources.title: Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism (Shoeybi et al.)
